 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Emmanuel Emegha has sent a clear message to Chelsea fans and his teammates ahead of the Blues' high-stakes encounter with Leeds United. The young striker, who recently made his first appearances for the club, is eager to secure a starting role and make a lasting impression at Stamford Bridge.
 Emegha ready for Stamford Bridge breakthrough
 Emegha is growing increasingly confident about his prospects at Chelsea as he prepares for a potential impact against Leeds United. The 23-year-old forward has been integrating into the first-team squad following his recent debut, and he believes his energy will soon become a focal point for the home supporters at Stamford Bridge. Having tasted his first minutes of action before the recent international break, the former Strasbourg man is eager to cement his place in the side.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I know that, when my time comes, I will be ready, and I know that the stadium will love my energy," said Emegha on the club's official website .
 Relishing fierce competition at Cobham
 The striker's self-assurance comes at a time when the Blues are looking to sharpen their attacking options for a busy winter period . He appears unfazed by the competition for places, instead viewing the high standards at Cobham as a necessary catalyst for his own professional development. The Dutchman admitted that the quality within the current Chelsea dressing room surpassed even his own lofty expectations.
 "I like it here – I'm in a room full of such talented players, it's not normal! Before coming, I knew that I could expect a high level, but I didn't know that it would be so crazy high. But I'm enjoying it. I'm getting better. I'm learning every single day," the forward explained.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A nomadic journey to the Premier League
 Emegha's path to one of world football's biggest stages has been far from conventional, involving stints in the Netherlands, Belgium, Austria, and France. This nomadic career start began with kickabouts in The Hague alongside his twin brother, but it eventually provided him with the mental resilience needed to survive in the English top flight. The striker credits these varied cultural experiences with helping him understand the necessity of personal growth and flexibility when joining a new club.
 "If you go to another country, you need to adapt to the country. The country will not adapt to you, and that's what I had to learn from very young," Emegha noted.
 Preparation for the Leeds United showdown
 The atmosphere at Stamford Bridge is expected to be electric as Leeds visit for another chapter in this fierce rivalry. Chelsea's preparations have been intense, with the squad welcoming back their international stars for final tactical sessions. For Emegha, the goal is simple: ensure he is the sharpest tool in Maresca's shed if called upon to lead the line or provide an injection of power from the substitutes' bench.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement With January fixtures already being moved for television coverage and the club building momentum, every minute on the pitch is vital for the young Dutchman. He remains focused on his daily improvement, confident that his unique blend of European experience and raw athleticism will eventually make him a household name in the Premier League.
